source_text: In inscriptione titulorum (fragmenta) ΕΙΣ ΤΑΣ ΕΠΙΓΡΑΦΑΣ ΤΗΣ ΣΤΗΛΟΓΡΑΦΙΑΣ 7 Φαίνεται τοίνυν ὅτι διττὰς ὑποτίθεται στηλῶν ἰδέας· οὐ γὰρ ἂν τὴν τοῦ Ἰακὼβ ἀποδεχόμενος εὐφήμως, ἐπετίμα τὰς τῶν ἐναντίων ὡς ἀσεβῶς ἱδρυμένας· ἀλλ' ἐκεῖναι μὲν εἰδωλολατρείας ἐκτυποῦσι φάσματα δαιμονιώδη κακοδόξως· ἡ δὲ τοῦ προπάτορος Ἰακὼβ, οὐ τὴν αὐτὴν ἐκείναις ἐμφαίνει πραγματείαν· ὁ γάρ τοι δίκαιος ἀνὴρ, ἐνηχηθεὶς ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, πρῶτον μὲν αὐτὸ τὸ σωματικὸν εἶδος ὁρᾷ τοῦ Χριστοῦ προαναζωγραφούμενον ἐναργῶς, ὅπερ ἐστὶν ὁρατὸν καὶ τοπικῆς ἐχόμενον περιγραφῆς· δεύτερον δὲ καὶ τὸ νικηφόρον τοῦ σταυροῦ τρόπαιον, κλίμακι προσεμφερῶς ἀπεικαζόμενον, ἱστορεῖ. Τούτῳ γὰρ καὶ ἐπεστηρίχθη μετεώρως ἑλκύσας ἅπαντας πρὸς ἑαυτόν.
thought_title: Jacob's pillar versus the pillars of his opponents
orientation: The author is opening his treatise by distinguishing Jacob's pillar at Bethel from the pillars of Jacob's opponents, arguing that Jacob's was a prophecy of Christ and the cross.
pass_a_gloss: It appears then that he supposes two kinds of pillars; for not, [if he were] accepting the [pillar] of Jacob with good words, would he have rebuked the [pillars] of the opponents as impiously set up; but those [pillars] imprint idolatry's demonic phantoms with evil opinion; but the [pillar] of the forefather Jacob does not show the same business as those; for the righteous man, having been sounded in by the Holy Spirit, first sees the very bodily form of Christ being prefigured clearly, which is visible and spatially limited; second he also recounts the victory-bearing trophy, the cross, being likened similarly to a ladder. For by this [trophy] he was also raised on high, having drawn all people to himself.

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'pillar' for στήλη, avoiding 'stele' or 'column'.
The glossary mandates 'ladder' for κλῖμαξ, avoiding 'stairway' or 'scala'.
The glossary mandates 'cross' for σταυρός, avoiding 'stake' or 'tree'.
The glossary mandates 'trophy' for τρόπαιον, avoiding 'victory monument' or 'standard'.
The glossary mandates 'idolatry' for εἰδωλολατρεία, avoiding 'idol worship' or 'image-worship'.

choices.english: having been sounded in by the Holy Spirit
choices.why: Renders the passive participle with the dative of agent literally, preserving the metaphor of divine inspiration as a sounding-in.

pass_b_english: It is clear, then, that he assumes two kinds of pillars. For he would not have accepted Jacob's pillar with approval while rebuking those of his opponents as impiously erected. Those pillars imprint demonic phantoms of idolatry with impious belief, but the pillar of the forefather Jacob does not display the same activity as those. For the righteous man, having been inspired by the Holy Spirit, first sees the very bodily form of Christ being vividly pre-painted beforehand, which is visible and subject to local circumscription. Second, he also depicts the victory-bearing trophy of the cross, likened in a manner resembling a ladder. For by this it was also firmly set on high, drawing all people to itself.

problems.quote: having been sounded in by the Holy Spirit
problems.why: "Sounded in" is not English idiom; ἐνηχηθεὶς means inspired/moved by, not acoustically sounded.
problems.fix: having been inspired by the Holy Spirit

problems.why: κακοδόξως means 'with wrong/evil belief', i.e. heretically or impiously, not 'with evil intent'.
problems.ruling: κακοδόξως = 'with wrong belief/heretically' (δόξα = belief), not 'intent' (πρόθεσις). Meaning changed.

problems.why: Subject is wrong: the cross/trophy was raised, not Jacob; ἐπεστηρίχθη is passive.
problems.fix: For by this it was also raised aloft
problems.ruling: ἐπεστηρίχθη μετεώρως refers to the trophy/cross raised on high (John 12:32), not Jacob; passive subject is wrong.

edits.old: having been sounded in by the Holy Spirit
edits.new: having been inspired by the Holy Spirit

edits.old: For by this he was also raised on high, drawing all people to himself.
edits.new: For by this it was also raised aloft, drawing all people to himself.

problems.quote: by this it was also raised aloft
problems.why: Subject is Jacob/Christ, not the cross; ἐπεστηρίχθη means 'was supported/fixed firmly', passive of στηρίζω.
problems.fix: For by this he was also firmly set on high, drawing all people to himself
problems.ruling: ἐπεστηρίχθη (from στηρίζω) means 'was supported/fixed,' not 'raised aloft'; Τούτῳ likely refers to the cross, but rendering is wrong.

edits.old: For by this it was also raised aloft, drawing all people to himself.
edits.new: For by this he was also firmly set on high, drawing all people to himself.

fixed: The mistranslation of 'Τούτῳ γὰρ καὶ ἐπεστηρίχθη μετεώρως' is real: the subject is Jacob/Christ, not the cross, and the verb means 'was supported/fixed firmly'. Changed 'it was also raised aloft' to 'he was also firmly set on high'.

problems.why: The Greek participle ἑλκύσας agrees with the cross/trophy (neuter), not Christ; the cross draws all, not 'he himself.'
problems.ruling: ἑλκύσας ἅπαντας πρὸς ἑαυτόν: context is the cross/trophy drawing all, not Christ; 'he himself' misleads.

edits.old: For by this he was also firmly set on high, drawing all people to himself.
edits.new: For by this it was also firmly set on high, drawing all people to itself.

problems.quote: the victory-bearing trophy of the cross
problems.why: Reader may not connect 'trophy' to 'cross' as same referent; 'trophy' is technical term.
Technical theological term; in context means Christ's body was spatially located, anti-Arian point.
problems.fix: Gloss as 'located in a specific place' or 'spatially limited'.

problems.quote: first sees the very bodily form of Christ being vividly pre-painted beforehand, which is visible and subject to local circumscription
problems.why: 'Pre-painted beforehand' is awkward and 'local circumscription' is opaque to modern readers.
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'first sees the bodily form of Christ prefigured, which is visible and spatially limited.'

edits.old: the victory-bearing trophy of the cross
first sees the very bodily form of Christ being vividly pre-painted beforehand, which is visible and subject to local circumscription
edits.new: first sees the very bodily form of Christ vividly prefigured, which is visible and spatially limited

fixed: The English already says the same thing for 'having been inspired by the Holy Spirit'.
The English already says the same thing for 'with impious belief'.
The English already says the same thing for 'For by this it was also firmly set on high, drawing all people to itself.'

problems.why: First called 'victory-bearing trophy' then simply 'the cross'; reader may miss they're identical.

problems.quote: first sees the very bodily form of Christ being vividly pre-painted beforehand, which is visible and spatially limited
problems.why: 'Pre-painted beforehand' is redundant; 'which is visible and spatially limited' dangles unclearly.
problems.fix: 'first sees Christ's bodily form vividly prefigured, visible and limited in space'.

problems.why: 'Pre-painted' is anachronistic and awkward; Greek likely means 'prefigured' or 'depicted in advance'.

edits.old: first sees the very bodily form of Christ being vividly pre-painted beforehand, which is visible and spatially limited.
edits.new: first sees the very bodily form of Christ vividly prefigured, visible and limited in space.

edits.old: Second, he also depicts the victory-bearing trophy, the cross, likened in a manner resembling a ladder.
edits.new: Second, he also depicts the victory-bearing trophy of the cross, likened in a manner resembling a ladder.

fixed: The 'victory-bearing trophy, the cross' issue is resolved by using 'of the cross' to make the identity explicit.
The 'pre-painted beforehand' redundancy and dangling clause are fixed by replacing with 'vividly prefigured, visible and limited in space'.

last_rejected.why: "Pre-painted" is absurd; ζωγραφέω means to depict/draw, not paint with pigment. The sense is "prefigured" or "depicted beforehand."
last_rejected.ruling: ζωγραφέω literally means paint/draw; προ- adds 'beforehand.' 'Pre-painted' is unusual but within range, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: ἱστορεῖ means "narrates" or "records," not "depicts." Jacob narrates/describes what he sees, not creates a depiction.
last_rejected.ruling: ἱστορέω can mean 'inquire, narrate, record, depict.' 'Depicts' is within the word's semantic range here.

last_rejected.quote: it was also firmly set on high
last_rejected.why: The Greek says the cross/trophy was "set firmly aloft" or "established on high," but "it" is ambiguous; the subject is the trophy/cross, not the ladder. The syntax is slightly off.
last_rejected.fix: for this was firmly established aloft
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπεστηρίχθη μετεώρως = 'firmly set on high.' Pronoun 'it' naturally refers to trophy/cross; no meaning change or real error.
